title: Mirai Worm Investigation
description: Investigate a network compromised by the Mirai worm and perform incident response tasks to contain and analyze the infection.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Mirai worm is a well-known malware that turns networked devices running Linux into remotely controlled bots. It primarily targets online consumer devices such as IP cameras and home routers. The malware continuously scans the internet for vulnerable IoT devices using a table of common factory default usernames and passwords. In this scenario, you will investigate a network compromised by the Mirai worm and perform incident response tasks to contain and analyze the infection.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `patient-zero` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised network and perform necessary actions to contain the infection. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `patient-zero` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised network and perform necessary actions to contain the infection. Enter the word `start` to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious scheduled task/timer used by the malware for persistence
levels.content: The Mirai worm uses a scheduled task to maintain persistence on infected hosts. Investigate the systemd timers on the `patient-zero` host to identify the suspicious timer.
levels.solution: The suspicious timer is located in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory. The timer name is `sysnet-monitor.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for timers in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory.

levels.title: Identify the hidden malware directory used by the worm
levels.content: The Mirai worm creates a hidden directory to store its files. Investigate the filesystem on the `patient-zero` host to find this directory.
levels.solution: The hidden malware directory is located in `/opt/.worm`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check directories in `/opt/` for suspicious names.

levels.title: Identify the beaconing mechanism used by the worm to communicate with the command and control (C2) server
levels.content: The Mirai worm uses a beaconing mechanism to communicate with its C2 server. Investigate the scripts in the hidden malware directory on the `patient-zero` host to identify the beaconing script.
levels.solution: The beaconing script is located in `/opt/.worm/beacon.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts in the hidden malware directory that make network connections.
